label: misaligned
reason: The predicate checks only the geodesic equation for total coordinate functions and imposes no continuity or local chart-source containment on the underlying curve. On the real line with a valid atlas of restricted translation charts extended by zero outside their sources, a curve jumping from 0 to 1 has identically zero chartLocalCurve at every time. Zero velocity and acceleration satisfy all derivative conditions and the Christoffel equation, although the curve is discontinuous on an open interval and is not a smooth geodesic. As a complete geodesic definition, the predicate therefore accepts objects excluded by the source.
review_scope: Morgan-Tian Definition 1.17, interpreted as the complete predicate for smooth geodesics on an open interval; smoothness is not supplied as an unrecorded external precondition.

analysis.second_pass: The explicit smooth-atlas countermodel establishes that the chart equation does not imply continuity, even on an open interval in the ordinary connected, boundaryless real line. The derivative checks apply to constant coordinate functions and the Christoffel contraction vanishes for zero velocity, without needing a Christoffel computation. On curves independently assumed smooth the usual coordinate equation is correct, but the user confirmed the complete-predicate interpretation and the misaligned verdict after reviewing this distinction.

counterexample.status: Mathematical countermodel checked against the retained definitions and pinned mathlib structures; not a Lean-kernel-certified construction.
counterexample.ambient_space: E = H = M = real numbers with their ordinary topology; identity model with corners; a custom preferred atlas of restricted translation charts; the ordinary Euclidean Riemannian metric. The manifold is connected, Hausdorff, finite-dimensional and boundaryless.
counterexample.atlas: For each p in R, let U_p = (p-1/4,p+1/4) and V = (-1/4,1/4). The chart c_p has source U_p, target V, total forward function c_p(x) = x-p when x is in U_p and 0 otherwise, and total inverse c_p^{-1}(y) = p+y. Choose c_p as chartAt p and take all c_p as the atlas.
counterexample.atlas_validity: Restricted to U_p and V these maps are inverse homeomorphisms. Their values outside the source are unconstrained by PartialEquiv and PartialHomeomorph. On every chart overlap the transition c_q composed with c_p^{-1} is the translation y -> y+p-q, hence smooth. These charts therefore give the ordinary smooth structure. Preferred coordinate derivatives equal 1 locally, so the Euclidean metric is a smooth positive-definite bundle metric satisfying the formal hypotheses.
counterexample.curve: Take s = (-1,1) and define gamma(t) = 0 for t <= 0 and gamma(t) = 1 for t > 0, as a total map R -> M. It is discontinuous at the interior time 0.
counterexample.coordinate_calculation: c_0(0) = c_0(1) = c_1(0) = c_1(1) = 0. Therefore, for every fixed t, chartLocalCurve gamma t, namely u -> c_{gamma(t)}(gamma(u)), is identically zero on all of R.
counterexample.formal_predicate: At every t choose v = a = 0. Both HasDerivAt conditions hold for constant functions, and the eventual HasDerivAt condition holds everywhere. chartChristoffelContraction g (gamma(t)) 0 0 y = 0 directly from chartCoord(i,0)=0 and its bilinear summation formula, independently of the numerical Christoffel values. Thus HasGeodesicEquationAt holds at every t and IsGeodesicOn g gamma (-1,1) is true.
counterexample.separation: The curve is not continuous, hence not a smooth geodesic in the source definition. Coordinate regularity cannot recover manifold regularity without local source containment: near t=0 the curve jumps outside the chart at gamma(0), whose arbitrary total extension hides the jump.
counterexample.scope_limit: This separates the complete classifier on arbitrary curves, not its restriction to curves already assumed smooth. The interval is open and the failure occurs at an interior point, so no endpoint convention is involved.
